description: REQ-D1 pins compute_dormant_state placement 'between line 122 (STEP 3 recipe block end) and line 127 (SKIP guard read)', and REQ-D1a says time_horizon_days is read via 'resolve_time_horizon_days(menu, default=14) ... after menu is loaded at line 145.' BOTH line numbers are wrong and — worse — mutually incompatible with the actual dispatcher control flow verified at skills/_shared/proactive-loop-dispatch.py:115-184. Real line numbers: the STEP 3 recipe/health block ends at line 139 (the `except` handler), the SKIP guard reads `.dormant.sentinel` at line 147, and `menu = load_menu(...)` is at line 169 (AFTER the SKIP guard). REQ-D1 requires compute_dormant_state to run BEFORE the SKIP guard (so a sentinel written this tick short-circuits STEP 6 in the same tick), yet REQ-D1a requires `menu` to feed `resolve_time_horizon_days(menu)` — but `menu` is not loaded until line 169, i.e. AFTER the SKIP guard. As written, the spec is unimplementable: Phase 2/3 either (a) violates REQ-D1 (compute after SKIP → sentinel takes effect only next tick, defeating REQ-D1 rationale (b)), or (b) violates REQ-D1a (compute before menu load → time_horizon_days source undefined), or (c) silently moves the menu load, which is a spec change not authorized here. The spec must either (i) require moving `menu = load_menu(...)` above the SKIP guard AND fix all cited line numbers, or (ii) redefine the placement to be before-line-147 with an explicit early menu read. This defect blocks PROP-D1 and PROP-D2 from being unambiguously testable.
